thread:
mika: heads up — after the latest canary we saw KV prefix hit-rate drop from ~0.72 -> 0.21 for the recommendation model. latency p50 for short prompts jumped ~80ms.
ryan: ouch. any idea what changed? batching? kernels?
mika: preliminary profiler shows more small-token requests falling back to the generic matmul kernel (not the fused attention path) + continuous batching window widened. suspected cause: new batching heuristic combined with a tiny change in tokenization made prefix keys not match existing cached entries.
anya: do we have an example key mismatch? can we reproduce locally with a replay?
mika: yes — saved a trace. repro script attached in thread gist (I'll paste snippet):
```
# rough repro
curl -X POST https://canary-infer.local/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rec-2025","prompt":"User: Hi\nSystem: Recommend"}' 
# then replay same prompt -> old cache key expected 'rec-2025::md5(prefix-v1)::len12' but runtime generated 'rec-2025::md5(prefix-v2)::len12'
```
ryan: so keying version bumped? maybe kernel selection influences normalization (numpy vs torch tokenization rounding)?
samir: digging into code — we switched some string normalization to micro-optimizations that changed whitespace canonicalization (trim vs collapse). that would change MD5.
anya: ok that explains hit rate. but even with correct keys we still have warmup gap on autoscale events — cold hosts with empty KV. we need a safe, low-cost prepopulate plan.
mika: proposal: deploy-time light seeders + autoscale ramp probes + tenant-aware scheduled primes. specifics:
  - deploy-time: when a model version hits canary -> run N small seeder requests covering top 200 prefixes (from last 7 days) distributed across hosts.
  - autoscale: on scale-up, run 5 synthetic probes per new replica that request most-likely prefixes (cheap tokens) under a low QPS limiter.
  - scheduled: nightly cron job for long-tail prefixes (rate-limited, batched).
ryan: 👍 keep probes cheap. important: probes must not affect billing/metrics or evict hot KV. maybe use ephemeral namespace or tag entries with primed=true and lower eviction priority.
samir: infra concern: how to authenticate synthetic traffic without polluting logs? infra-bot can issue a short-lived seed token scoped to priming ops and a log flag. infra-bot: created seed-token flow for this; logs will be labeled "priming" and filtered in billing pipeline.
anya: also need rollback plan: if seeder causes regressions, we should be able to disable per-model priming via a flag.
mika: agreed. action items:
  - samir: implement seed-token + log filter (ETA 1d)
  - ryan: add seeding hooks to deploy pipeline + limiter config (ETA 2d)
  - anya: craft prefix selection heuristic for top-200 and long-tail sampler + metric dashboard (ETA 3d)
  - mika: run controlled canary with seeding on next deploy and collect hit-rate/latency deltas.
ryan: one more: add a tiny kernel-selection unit test to ensure token normalization is stable across code paths.
anya: will do.
mika: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review canary data. :thumbsup:
